MARKET OVERVIEW

1. What is the Current Market Regime?
RISK-ON: normal volatility at 32.1% and strong breadth, with 7/8 sectors positive over 1W. Participation is broad, though most sectors remain negative over 1M.

2. Which sectors are leading?
Technology & Telecom leads on a 1W basis (+21.59%), led by KONTR (1W: +59.88% | 1M: +21.92%), ABOVE TREND. Transportation is next (+15.70%), with THYAO (1W: +17.62% | 1M: +2.24%), ABOVE TREND, and PGSUS (1W: +15.14% | 1M: -0.21%), RECOVERY.

3. Which sectors are lagging?
Heavy Industry is the only sector negative over 1W (-0.80%) and is also weakest over 1M (-16.14%). Weakness includes ASELS (1W: -8.23% | 1M: -12.50%), BELOW TREND, and TOASO (1W: -3.17% | 1M: -17.90%), BELOW TREND.

STOCK PERFORMANCE

4. Top Performing Stocks?
The top five 1W performers are KONTR (1W: +59.88% | 1M: +21.92%), ABOVE TREND; THYAO (1W: +17.62% | 1M: +2.24%), ABOVE TREND; HEKTS (1W: +15.19% | 1M: -16.89%), RECOVERY; PGSUS (1W: +15.14% | 1M: -0.21%), RECOVERY; and TSKB (1W: +15.06% | 1M: +2.71%), ABOVE TREND.

5. Worst Performing Stocks?
The weakest five on 1W are ASELS (1W: -8.23% | 1M: -12.50%), BELOW TREND; CCOLA (1W: -7.14% | 1M: -14.43%), BELOW TREND; HALKB (1W: -7.05% | 1M: -11.36%), BELOW TREND; TUPRS (1W: -6.55% | 1M: -12.52%), BELOW TREND; and TOASO (1W: -3.17% | 1M: -17.90%), BELOW TREND.

6. Momentum Stocks?
Weekly momentum is led by KONTR (1W: +59.88% | 1M: +21.92%), ABOVE TREND, followed by THYAO (1W: +17.62% | 1M: +2.24%), ABOVE TREND, HEKTS (1W: +15.19% | 1M: -16.89%), RECOVERY, PGSUS (1W: +15.14% | 1M: -0.21%), RECOVERY, and TSKB (1W: +15.06% | 1M: +2.71%), ABOVE TREND. The sharpest rebounds are concentrated in names whose 1M performance remains negative.

SECTOR OUTLOOK

7. Banking Sector Outlook?
Banking gained 6.31% over 1W, while its 1M return remains -1.12%. GARAN (1W: +12.08% | 1M: +8.23%), ABOVE TREND, leads; AKBNK (1W: +6.67% | 1M: -3.31%), RECOVERY, contrasts with HALKB (1W: -7.05% | 1M: -11.36%), BELOW TREND.

8. Industrial Sector Outlook?
Heavy Industry remains under pressure, down 0.80% over 1W and 16.14% over 1M. EREGL (1W: -1.35% | 1M: -16.94%), BELOW TREND, FROTO (1W: -1.95% | 1M: -9.05%), BELOW TREND, and ASELS (1W: -8.23% | 1M: -12.50%), BELOW TREND, show no confirmed turn.

9. Energy & Chemicals Outlook?
The sector is up 4.34% over 1W but down 14.25% over 1M, indicating a short-term rebound within a weak monthly trend. HEKTS (1W: +15.19% | 1M: -16.89%), RECOVERY, and SASA (1W: +9.40% | 1M: -14.21%), RECOVERY, lead the bounce; TUPRS (1W: -6.55% | 1M: -12.52%), BELOW TREND, and PETKM (1W: -3.54% | 1M: -14.66%), BELOW TREND, lag.

PORTFOLIO STRATEGY

10. Portfolio Recommendation?
Maintain a selective risk-on stance: favor confirmed strength and broad participation, but avoid treating sharp RECOVERY moves as established uptrends. Keep exposure disciplined given the 32.1% volatility and persistent 1M weakness across several sectors.

NEXT WEEK OUTLOOK

11. Stocks to Watch Next Week?
Track KONTR (1W: +59.88% | 1M: +21.92%), ABOVE TREND, for continuation after its outsized surge; GARAN (1W: +12.08% | 1M: +8.23%), ABOVE TREND, for banking follow-through; and THYAO (1W: +17.62% | 1M: +2.24%), ABOVE TREND, for transport momentum. HEKTS (1W: +15.19% | 1M: -16.89%), RECOVERY, and PGSUS (1W: +15.14% | 1M: -0.21%), RECOVERY, are rebound tests.

12. Sectors to Watch Next Week?
Monitor Technology & Telecom and Transportation for continuation after the strongest weekly gains, and Banking for confirmation of its rebound. Heavy Industry remains the key downside risk, with the sector the only one negative over 1W.

13. Key Levels & Triggers?
No XU100 price levels or catalyst calendar were provided, so specific support, resistance, or event levels cannot be verified. Watch whether breadth holds near 7/8 positive and whether volatility stays around the normal 32.1% regime.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The market is RISK-ON, supported by normal volatility and broad weekly participation, with Technology & Telecom and Transportation leading. Momentum is strong but uneven: several rebound leaders remain negative over 1M, while Heavy Industry continues to lag.
